display.purpose: Rare onboarding, empty-state, or route-level moments. Never in dense UI.

headline.purpose: Page headings and workflow section leads.

title.purpose: Panels, drawers, record groups, and dialogs.

body.purpose: Explanatory copy and record summaries. Cap prose at 65-75ch.

label.purpose: Eyebrows, metadata labels, sidebar headings, table headers, sync labels.

shadows.name: legacy-ambient-panel
shadows.purpose: Existing web shell panel shadow. Do not expand as a default pattern.

shadows.name: floating-map-control
shadows.purpose: Controls genuinely floating over live basemap tiles. The one place backdrop-blur is also earned.

shadows.name: backdrop-scrim
shadows.purpose: Modal drawer backdrop for committed interruption.

motion.name: motion-standard
motion.purpose: Default state transition. Product register caps most transitions at 150-250ms.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default easing. Exponential ease-out; no bounce, no elastic.

stacking.name: pinned
stacking.purpose: Sticky panel headers, map overlays, floating map controls.

stacking.name: overlay
stacking.purpose: Dialogs, drawers, popovers, tooltips, toasts, skip link.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The committed action. Once per local workflow where possible.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; gap:8px; height:36px; padding:0 16px; border:none; border-radius:var(--radius,8px); background:var(--primary,#0c5331); color:var(--primary-foreground,#f5faf7); font:500 14px/1 Poppins,ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif; cursor:pointer; transition:background 180ms cubic-bezier(0.25,1,0.5,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background:color-mix(in oklch, var(--primary,#0c5331) 90%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline:none; box-shadow:0 0 0 3px var(--ring,#907813); } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity:.5; pointer-events:none; }

components.name: Destructive Button
components.description: Irreversible actions. Uses the semantic destructive token, which is a shade below brand Alert Red so white text clears AA (5.63:1).
components.css: .ds-btn-destructive { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; gap:8px; height:36px; padding:0 16px; border:none; border-radius:var(--radius,8px); background:var(--destructive,#c81f42); color:#fff; font:500 14px/1 Poppins,ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif; cursor:pointer; transition:background 180ms cubic-bezier(0.25,1,0.5,1); } .ds-btn-destructive:hover { background:color-mix(in oklch, var(--destructive,#c81f42) 90%, transparent); } .ds-btn-destructive:focus-visible { outline:none; box-shadow:0 0 0 3px var(--destructive,#c81f42); }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Navigation, row actions, and cancellation-like commands.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; gap:8px; height:36px; padding:0 16px; border:1px solid var(--border,#a7bfba); border-radius:var(--radius,8px); background:var(--background,#f0fbf4); color:var(--foreground,#102325); font:500 14px/1 Poppins,ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif; cursor:pointer; transition:background 180ms cubic-bezier(0.25,1,0.5,1); } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background:var(--accent,#f5f6ce); color:var(--accent-foreground,#053d22); } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline:none; border-color:var(--ring,#907813); box-shadow:0 0 0 3px var(--ring,#907813); }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Surface background, Border Strong stroke. The stroke is a control boundary and clears 3:1; focus draws a solid Deep Pollen ring.
components.html: <input class="ds-input" type="text" placeholder="Search name or description…" />
components.css: .ds-input { width:100%; height:36px; padding:4px 12px; border:1px solid var(--input,#679082); border-radius:var(--radius,8px); background:var(--card,#f9fdfb); color:var(--foreground,#102325); font:400 14px/1.4 Poppins,ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif; outline:none; transition:box-shadow 180ms cubic-bezier(0.25,1,0.5,1); } .ds-input::placeholder { color:var(--muted-foreground,#4b6265); } .ds-input:focus-visible { border-color:var(--ring,#907813); box-shadow:0 0 0 3px var(--ring,#907813); } .ds-input[aria-invalid="true"] { border-color:var(--destructive,#c81f42); }

components.name: Field Error
components.description: Validation message under a control. role="alert", wired via aria-describedby by the shared FormFieldFrame. 5.49:1 on card at 14px.

components.name: Sticky Panel Header
components.description: Pinned bar atop a scrolling panel. Opaque by rule — no backdrop-blur, because nothing moves behind it.
components.css: .ds-sticky-header { position:sticky; top:0; z-index:10; display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:space-between; gap:12px; padding:16px; background:var(--background,#f0fbf4); border-bottom:1px solid color-mix(in oklch, var(--border,#a7bfba) 50%, transparent); } .ds-sticky-title { font:700 18px/1.25 Poppins,ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif; color:var(--foreground,#102325); } .ds-sticky-meta { font:400 12px/1.2 Poppins,ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif; color:var(--muted-foreground,#4b6265); }

components.name: Rail Icon (dark chrome)
components.description: Primary rail item on the deep-green chrome. Demonstrates the inverse focus ring: Deep Pollen would only reach 3.7:1 here, Bright Pollen reaches 10.4:1.
components.css: .ds-rail { display:flex; padding:12px; background:var(--simmer-green-900,#032815); } .ds-rail-item { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; width:44px; height:44px; border:none; border-radius:var(--radius,8px); background:rgba(255,255,255,0.06); color:#e7faed; cursor:pointer; transition:background 120ms cubic-bezier(0.25,1,0.5,1); } .ds-rail-item:hover { background:rgba(255,255,255,0.14); } .ds-rail-item:focus-visible { outline:none; box-shadow:0 0 0 2px var(--simmer-green-900,#032815), 0 0 0 4px var(--ring-inverse,#ddd474); }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: Record status on list rows. Status is carried by icon plus text, never colour alone.
components.html: Active
components.css: .ds-badge { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:4px; padding:2px 8px; border:1px solid color-mix(in oklch, var(--success,#0c5331) 25%, transparent); border-radius:999px; background:var(--success-bg,#cff1da); color:var(--success,#0c5331); font:500 12px/1.4 Poppins,ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif; }

narrative.overview:
SIMMER should feel like a calm operational workspace built around geography: professional, natural, and focused. It is not a marketing surface and not a generic admin console. It is where agency and SIMMER Operator work becomes legible enough to trust.

The product register is restrained, but not bland. Use tinted neutrals, grounded green, and earned yellow attention to keep dense workflows readable. The interface should feel field-aware through language, structure, map adjacency, and record relationships, not through decorative nature motifs.

The system explicitly rejects generic government portal design, enterprise GIS clone density, dashboard theater, consumer map mimicry, and table-first data representation. When in doubt, make the next operational action clearer.
keyCharacteristics: Restrained product surfaces with warm field cues.
Visual representations before tables when location, time, status, or relationships explain the work better.
Durable tokens in packages/design-tokens, shadcn source components in packages/ui-web, cva variants for repeated styles, then route-level styling only as a last resort.
Desktop-only by decision, with an explicit width floor rather than an implied mobile promise.

rules.name: The Earned Color Rule
rules.body: Every non-neutral color must carry a semantic job: action, status, selection, focus, taxonomy, sync, or spatial meaning.

rules.name: The Map-Room Neutral Rule
rules.body: Neutral surfaces are tinted toward green and blue. Never use pure black or pure white.

rules.name: The No Decoration Rule
rules.body: Product screens use color to clarify work, not to fill empty space.

rules.name: The State Colour Rule
rules.body: A colour that only appears under a condition — focus, error, invalid, inactive, selected — is the one that will ship broken. Prove state colours with a measured ratio, not an eye.

rules.name: The Solid Indicator Rule
rules.body: A focus ring is never drawn at partial alpha. An alpha ring composites toward the surface it is supposed to contrast against.

rules.name: The Poppins Rule
rules.body: Poppins is the intended SIMMER sans serif. Replace current Inter/system stacks as product surfaces are touched.

rules.name: The Product Type Rule
rules.body: Typography must help users scan and act. Do not use display styling in labels, buttons, tables, forms, or dense controls.

rules.name: The Flat Until Floating Rule
rules.body: Resting surfaces are flat. Floating surfaces must earn depth by interrupting, overlaying, or anchoring to a map/task context.

rules.name: The Opaque Pin Rule
rules.body: A sticky header is fully opaque. A blur behind an opaque surface is decoration with a compositing cost.

rules.name: The Desktop Floor Rule
rules.body: SIMMER web is a desktop application. Both rails stay visible at every width; below the floor the page takes a horizontal scrollbar rather than reflowing.

rules.name: The One Selection Rule
rules.body: Selection is amber everywhere, on every layer, and matches what the draw tool paints.

rules.name: The Legend Truth Rule
rules.body: A map legend reads its swatches from the same constants the layers paint with. Never a literal.

dos: Do keep SIMMER Green and SIMMER Yellow stable across every platform.
Do use Poppins as the SIMMER sans serif when touching product surfaces.
Do use OKLCH for CSS tokens and keep neutrals tinted, never pure black or pure white.
Do preserve the map as operational context wherever spatial work is the user’s job.
Do use visual representations before tables when maps, timelines, status grouping, spatial overlays, compact summaries, or record relationships clarify the work.
Do centralize durable choices in packages/design-tokens and component variants.
Do use shadcn source components from packages/ui-web wherever possible, styled with Tailwind semantic tokens.
Do add repeated states, sizes, and visual treatments as cva variants and compose classes with cn.
Do treat SIMMER Operator screens as product-quality surfaces, not temporary scaffolding.
Do prove state colours (focus, error, invalid, inactive, selected) with a measured contrast ratio, not an eye.
Do draw focus rings solid, and use the inverse ring on dark chrome.
Do read map legend swatches from map-palette constants, never literals.
Do delete a superseded module when its last caller goes.
donts: Don’t make generic government portal design: boxy forms, weak hierarchy, dated chrome, or administrative leftovers.
Don’t become an enterprise GIS clone: dense toolbars, overwhelming layer panels, crowded controls, or "ArcGIS but worse" interactions.
Don’t use dashboard theater: excessive metric cards, generic chart blocks, gradient SaaS decoration, or analytics surfaces that exist because dashboards are expected.
Don’t mimic consumer maps so closely that SIMMER becomes too casual, too search-first, or too shallow for operational record keeping.
Don’t default to table-first data representation when spatial, temporal, status, or relationship views explain the work more directly.
Don’t build CSS-only replicas of shadcn primitives.
Don’t scatter repeated color, typography, border, radius, shadow, focus, or animation classes through app routes when a token or cva component variant can own the decision.
Don’t use colored side-stripe borders, gradient text, decorative glassmorphism, identical card grids, or modals as the first design answer.
Don’t draw a focus ring, or any indicator that must clear a contrast threshold, at partial alpha.
Don’t put a backdrop-blur behind a surface that is already opaque.
Don’t let a small utility that eager code imports share a module with a heavy component.
Don’t assume a phone-width viewport is a supported layout target.
